target_customer: Companies in Latin America (fintechs, remittance and wallet apps, businesses with cross-border flows) that want to use crypto and stablecoin rails through an API
problem: Moving money between local Latin American currencies and digital dollars or crypto is fragmented, hard to integrate and compliance heavy for non-specialist companies.
business_model: Usage-based payments API and treasury platform with transaction fees on on-ramp, off-ramp and OTC flows
product_category: Crypto and stablecoin on and off ramp, payments API

founders.name: Ignacio Detmer
prior_employers: Americas Car Group (co-founder and COO, per YC page)
previous_startups: Americas Car Group (sold to Prosus Group, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Education not stated on the YC page.

founders.name: Guillermo Acuña
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a Chilean entrepreneur and fullstack handyman; no employers or education given.

competitors.name: Bitso
competitors.what: Mexico-based crypto exchange with a Latin American customer base and a business arm
competitors.traction_then: Said it doubled its Latin America customer base in the past year (2022 coverage)

technical_complexity.rationale: API wrappers over local banking rails, KYC and custody in several countries. Hard parts were compliance and integrations per country rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Local licences, bank connections and compliance work in each market take time to replicate, but the product category was contested by larger exchanges.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large regional exchanges already sold business on and off ramp services. No source shows them absorbing Koywe; Koywe itself bought Facto in 2024.

market_need_then: Chainalysis data cited in 2022 coverage put Latin America at 9.1 percent of global crypto value received, and remittances are a large use case in the region.

identity.voice_and_tone: Corporate treasury and payments voice on the current site.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. The name is unusual and easily confused with Koyeb in search results.

pivots.from: Crypto on and off ramp API for Latin American companies
pivots.to: International treasury platform with stablecoins, OTC desk and payments
pivots.why: Not stated; positioning on the current website differs from the YC page

outcome_analysis: Koywe is still active and has stayed small. It raised a seed in January 2023, then bought the US invoicing startup Facto in mid 2024, and describes itself as a treasury platform across five Latin American markets. Funding detail beyond the seed is only in aggregators, so the real trajectory is unclear.
notes: Seed amount conflicts: Contxto (June 2024) says 2.5M USD, a law firm item says 1.1M USD convertible note and SAFE, so no amount recorded. Seed investors named only in a Medium/aggregator snippet (Manutara, Daedalus, Rhombuz), unverified. Aggregators list a 5M USD round in Aug or Sep 2024 labelled Seed or Series A II and totals from 1.6M to 14.6M USD; all unverified. Facto acquisition (terms undisclosed) reported June 2024. No dated competitor sources from the batch period other than Bitso. Name origin searched and not found.
